questions.q: Why would Northbridge use Azure Container Registry instead of Docker Hub for the catalog service's production images?
options: Docker Hub cannot store private images under any circumstances
ACR is required before a Dockerfile can be built
ACR lives inside their own Azure subscription and authenticates through the same Azure identity (IAM) that already controls their AKS cluster
ACR is the only registry that supports image tags
questions.explain: ACR's main advantage for a team already on Azure is that it plugs directly into existing Azure IAM and infrastructure, rather than requiring a separate Docker Hub account.

questions.q: What does `az acr login --name northbridgeacr` actually do?
options: Creates a brand-new Azure subscription
Deletes all images currently stored in the registry
Authenticates Docker against the ACR registry using the Azure CLI session that's already signed in
Builds a Docker image from the current directory
questions.explain: az acr login connects Docker's authentication to the existing Azure CLI session, the same role docker login plays for Docker Hub -- just backed by Azure identity.

questions.q: What does `aws ecr get-login-password` return, and what is it used for?
options: The IP address of the ECR registry
A short-lived authentication token, piped into `docker login` to authenticate against ECR
A list of every image stored in the repository
A permanent password that never needs to be refreshed
questions.explain: aws ecr get-login-password returns a temporary token (valid for 12 hours) that gets piped straight into docker login instead of typing a password manually.

questions.q: Before an image can be pushed to ACR or ECR, what must it be tagged with?
options: The registry's own hostname, such as `northbridgeacr.azurecr.io` or `<account-id>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com`
Nothing -- docker push works without any tag at all
The name of the Azure resource group only
A random UUID generated by Docker
questions.explain: Just like Docker Hub in Lesson 16, docker push reads its destination from the image's tag -- which must be prefixed with the target registry's own hostname.

questions.q: What is the common shape shared by pushing to Docker Hub, ACR, and ECR?
options: Authenticate against the registry, tag the image with that registry's namespace or hostname, then push
Only Docker Hub requires authentication; ACR and ECR do not
Each requires a completely unrelated process with no overlap
Images must be rebuilt from scratch for each registry
questions.explain: All three follow the same authenticate -> tag -> push pattern from Lesson 16, just with different login commands (docker login, az acr login, aws ecr get-login-password piped to docker login) standing in for each other.
